title: The waist: one module owns an id
objective: One module, `intentsvcs::id`, owns the ordinal id end to end behind typed ids, with every site in the workspace routed through it and no behaviour changed.
body:
Seat: cc. Size: L.

## Scope

- Register `intentsvcs::id` in `intent/llm/MODULES.md` first. It absorbs `model.rs`'s id section (`:55-60`, `:124-254`, `:296-509`).
- `ThreadId`, `WpId` and `IssueId`, each over one form that is an ordinal today and can hold a hash later, with no constructor outside the module. They replace `Thread.id: String` (`model.rs:564`), `WorkPackage.seq: u32` (`:1009`), `Issue.number: u32` (`:2065`) and `Related.id` (`:974`).
- Every site the compiler then lists: about 70 hand formatters in 17 files (ic's census, section 1, banked under `refs/bank/ic/st0095/`), the store's numeric bindings, ingest, export, renumber and doctor (cc's census, section 4, banked under `refs/bank/cc/st0095/`), and intent-cli's `render.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `show.rs` and `tui/app.rs`. cc converts the whole workspace in this one unit, and ic reads intent-cli's part.
- The module's duties in `design.md`, "One home: the waist", for the ordinal family: one stored-form reader, the pure operator reader, one formatter with each rendered form, one order, one text scanner in place of three, and the forms sentence.
- Two duplicates go first: the fiat cascade's inline copy of `contract::group_of` (`facade.rs:19703-19710`), and an issue's search owner spelled `703` (`ingest.rs:1859`) where everything else spells `0703`.
- The 37 test files that pass a number where an id is meant change type with it.

## Out of scope

- Any new family, any format change in the canon or the store, any new verb.

## Order

After WP-01, and before everything else of cc's.

## Proof

Today's suite passes unchanged through the cut's own gate, and an existing project's `intent sync` plans nothing after the build. `legacy.rs` calls the ordinal predicate and never a widened one.
